title: Where to Stay in Karlovac, Croatia: Best Areas 2027
metaDescription: Where to stay in Karlovac: Zvijezda old town, Korana riverbank, Dubovac and the outskirts compared, with real hotels, euro prices and local tips.
content:
## Best Areas to Stay in Karlovac

Karlovac is a small, flat city of about 55,000 people, built in 1579 as a star-shaped Habsburg fortress. It sits on four rivers: the Kupa, Korana, Mrežnica and Dobra. Most visitors cover the core on foot in half a day, so the neighbourhood choice comes down to atmosphere, parking and price rather than distance. Zagreb is about 55 km away, roughly 40 minutes by car.

### Zvijezda (Old Town): Best for First-Time Visitors

Zvijezda is the hexagonal historic core. Its grid of streets, the main square (Trg bana Josipa Jelačića), the Holy Trinity Church and the Franciscan Monastery are all within a 5–10 minute walk of each other. Cafés and restaurants cluster around the square and along Radićeva ulica, and the Habsburg-era facades give the area a tidy, Central European look.

- **Pros:** Everything is walkable, the evenings are lively by Karlovac standards, and the bus and train stations are close.
- **Cons:** Few large hotels sit directly inside the grid. Parking is paid in the central zones, and street spots fill up on market days.
- **Typical cost:** Apartments and small rooms run €50–80/night. Hotels at the edge of the core run €85–115.

### Korana Riverbank and Vrbanić Park: Best for a Quiet Upscale Stay

The Korana flows along the western side of the centre, and the Perivoj Josipa Vrbanića park runs beside it. Boutique Hotel Korana Srakovčić is here. It is a 4-star hotel with an indoor pool, a hot tub, free parking and breakfast. It is about a 10-minute walk from the Vrbanić gardens and Holy Trinity Church area. Rates generally sit at €105–130 per night and rise in September.

The riverside paths suit morning runs and walks, and the area is noticeably quieter at night than Zvijezda. This is the safest pick for couples, business travellers and anyone driving in.

### Dubovac: Best for Views and History

Dubovac is a hilltop district about 2–3 km from the centre, with a medieval castle of the Frankopan and Zrinski era. It has a village feel, a few private rooms and apartments, and views over the Kupa valley. Without a car, the walk down to the old town takes 30–40 minutes. Taxis or a bicycle make this workable. Choose Dubovac if you want peace and a short castle visit, not nightlife.

### Foginovo and the Aquatika Side: Best for Families

The Foginovo area, by the Kupa, is home to Aquatika, the freshwater aquarium that shows the fish of Croatia's rivers. Families who plan to visit the aquarium, and the riverside promenades can find apartments here that cost less than rooms in the core. Expect €45–70/night for a two-bed apartment. A short walk or 5-minute drive brings you back to the centre.

### Edges of the City and Main Roads: Best for Budget and Drivers

Budget hotels, motels and pensions line the roads leaving the centre. Hotel Srakovčić Heart of Nature is a 3-star option that often runs €45–55 per night. Motel Kod Bakija and Guesthouse Kod Mosta have been noted for free parking. Hostel Eva and Pansion Šu-Šu are cheaper beds for backpackers and cyclists. A car is useful here. Walking to the old town can take 20 minutes or more.

## Best Hotels in Karlovac by Type

### Best Overall: Boutique Hotel Korana Srakovčić

It has the strongest facilities in the city, with a pool, hot tub, parking and breakfast included in many rates. Rooms start around €105, and superior rooms are often cheaper than standard ones on booking sites, so compare room types.

### Best Value Mid-Range: Aminess Kadoor Hotel

Guests rate it 8.6/10 on Booking, with prices from about €75–95. It is one of the most booked hotels in the city, and breakfast gets steady praise.

### Best for Couples and Families: Aminess Florian & Godler Hotel

It gets good marks from couples and families, plus well-reviewed breakfast. Expect around €100–115 in a normal month.

### Best Practical Stay: Hotel Carlstadt

A 3-star with free parking, Wi-Fi and breakfast. The Booking score of 7.3/10 reflects older rooms, so treat it as a functional base, not a highlight.

### Best Budget: Heart of Nature, Hostel Eva and Guesthouses

These cover the €25–55 range. Check the exact distance to the centre before booking.

## Which Area Fits Which Traveller?

| Traveller | Best area |
|---|---|
| First visit, no car | Zvijezda |
| Quiet, pool, parking | Korana riverbank |
| Scenery and castle | Dubovac |
| Families with kids | Foginovo / Aquatika side |
| Tight budget | City edges |

## Prices and Seasons

- **Summer (June–August):** Karlovac is a stopover city, so prices stay moderate. Most 3–4 star hotels run €75–130.
- **September:** The peak for hotels such as Korana Srakovčić, and the most expensive month there.
- **October and winter:** About 20% cheaper. Weekend nights are sometimes lower than weeknights, because business travellers fill weekday rooms.
- **Advent:** The Karlovac Advent programme brings a short spike in demand, so book early.
- **Tourist tax:** A small per-person nightly tax of about €1–2 is added to many bills.

## Local Tips for Choosing Where to Stay

- Karlovac's beer, Karlovačko, is brewed in the city. The old-town cafés are the right place for it, not the roadside restaurants.
- The Mrežnica and Korana are the draw for canoeing and swimming in summer. Pick accommodation with parking if you plan river trips, since the access points are outside the centre.
- Many visitors only overnight on the way to the coast. Choose a hotel with free parking and an early breakfast to leave by 8:00 and avoid the A1 motorway queues.
- Skip a room right on the main trunk roads if you are a light sleeper. Lorries use them all night.
- Staying in the old town on a Saturday morning lets you reach the market early for fresh produce.

### A Plain Opinion

Booking a hotel on the edge of town because it saves €20 is rarely worth it. Zvijezda and the Korana riverbank are small enough that an extra €20 buys you a walk to dinner and a drink, and you skip taxi fares and parking hunts.

## Getting Around From Your Base

Karlovac has no metro, and the centre is covered on foot. Local city buses cover the suburbs. Taxis in town typically cost €5–10. The train and bus stations are at the edge of the core and connect to Zagreb in 45–60 minutes. A bicycle is the best way to reach the riverbanks and Dubovac.

## Booking Advice

1. Check whether breakfast is included. It often is at the 4-star level.
2. Confirm parking. Free parking is common at hotels but rare for old-town apartments.
3. Compare room types, since superior rooms can be cheaper than standard ones on some sites.
4. Book for September and Advent a few weeks in advance. Other months rarely sell out.

faq.question: What is the best area to stay in Karlovac?
faq.answer: Zvijezda, the star-shaped old town, is the best area for most visitors because the sights, cafés and stations are all within walking distance. The Korana riverbank near Vrbanić Park is better if you prefer quiet and want hotel facilities like a pool.

faq.question: How much does a hotel in Karlovac cost per night?
faq.answer: Budget hotels and guesthouses start around €25–55, mid-range hotels cost about €75–100, and the 4-star Korana Srakovčić runs about €105–130. Prices are lowest in October and winter and highest in September.

faq.question: Is Karlovac a good place to stay overnight?
faq.answer: Yes, for one or two nights. The compact old town, riverside walks and the Aquatika aquarium fill a day, and Zagreb is about 55 km away. It is a calmer, cheaper base than the capital.

faq.question: Which hotel in Karlovac has a pool?
faq.answer: Boutique Hotel Korana Srakovčić has an indoor pool and a hot tub. It also offers free parking and breakfast, and is on the Korana riverbank.

faq.question: Do I need a car if I stay in Karlovac?
faq.answer: Not in Zvijezda or near Vrbanić Park, where most sights are walkable. A car is helpful for Dubovac, the budget hotels on the edges of town and trips to the Mrežnica and Korana river access points.

faq.question: Is Karlovac good for families?
faq.answer: Yes. The Foginovo side has apartments near the Aquatika freshwater aquarium, and Aminess Florian & Godler Hotel is well reviewed by families. Riverside parks give children plenty of space.

faq.question: Is it cheaper to stay in Karlovac than in Zagreb?
faq.answer: Generally yes. Mid-range hotels in Karlovac run about €75–100, and Zagreb hotels are often higher in summer. The trip takes around 40 minutes by car or under an hour by train or bus.

quickAnswer: Stay in or next to Zvijezda, the star-shaped old town, for walkability and restaurants. Pick the Korana riverbank near Vrbanić Park for a quiet 4-star base (about €105–130/night). Budget travellers can choose guesthouses and hostels on the edges for €45–70. Dubovac suits a calm, scenic stay near the castle.
